sources.institution: INADUR / CEREN / PNUD; archived by INDECI BVPAD
sources.document: Mapa de peligros, plan de usos del suelo y plan de mitigacion de los efectos producidos por los desastres naturales en la ciudad de Paita
admissible_claims: Quebrada Nueva Esperanza, La Piscina, La Catarata, Villa Naval and El Zanjon are described as distinct local temporary drainage features in Paita
Nueva Esperanza is described as having originally drained toward El Zanjon, with urban construction modifying its course toward the 13 de Julio sector
La Piscina is described as having originally joined Nueva Esperanza and then El Zanjon
La Catarata is described as draining from Paita Alta toward El Zanjon
Villa Naval is described as draining toward the sea near the fishing complex, with a wall capable of diverting the path toward Puerto Nuevo
the local channels are temporary and respond to intense rainfall
forbidden_inferences: schematic or printed-map linework is reproducible child geometry without an independently frozen georeferencing method
a described drainage relationship supplies an exact confluence or outlet coordinate
a temporary channel description proves activation for an undated historical window
urban modification may be ignored when resolving current receiver connectivity
any named local channel shares an activation state with another channel

sources.institution: Municipalidad Provincial de Paita / CENEPRED SIGRID
sources.document: Plan de Prevencion y Reduccion del Riesgo de Desastres de la Provincia de Paita 2019-2021
admissible_claims: El Zanjon is described as draining most of Paita Baja through a canal-road toward the sea
the plan reports overflow of El Zanjon and extensive urban inundation during the 1983 El Nino event
La Piscina is described as draining through 13 de Julio toward El Zanjon
La Catarata is described as draining from Paita Alta toward El Zanjon
Villa Naval is described as draining toward the fishing-complex roadstead, with possible diversion toward Puerto Nuevo under severe El Nino conditions
the plan states that the 2017 event produced provincial impacts exceeding prior 1983 and 1998 events
the plan provides historical rainfall context for Paita including 1983 and 1998
forbidden_inferences: province-level 1998 impact context proves activation of any named Paita child
historical rainfall magnitudes become IRFEN decision thresholds
the canal-road description defines present hydraulic capacity
a mitigation structure or wall is historical channel capacity
susceptibility maps are observed event footprints
absence of a named-child report is a negative control

sources.document: Zonificacion sismica-geotecnica de la ciudad de Paita
admissible_claims: the study distinguishes fluvial and pluvial inundation mechanisms in Paita for the February-March 2017 rainfall period
it reports overflow from the left margin of El Zanjon before its mouth with flooding of Paita Baja and the historic urban core
it documents pluvial inundation in the upper urban setting as a distinct mechanism from El Zanjon overflow
forbidden_inferences: the 2017 El Zanjon observation proves activation of Nueva Esperanza, La Piscina, La Catarata or Villa Naval
an inundation depth reported by the provider becomes an IRFEN threshold
study figures are exact event footprints unless independently georeferenced and frozen
pluvial inundation and ravine overflow may be merged into one synthetic hydrologic child

sources.document: Informe de evaluacion del riesgo por inundacion pluvial en el centro poblado de Paita, distrito de Paita, provincia de Paita, departamento de Piura
admissible_claims: an official 2017 post-emergency risk evaluation exists for pluvial inundation in the urban center of Paita
forbidden_inferences: risk classes are IRFEN activation states or decision thresholds
risk polygons are observed 2017 event footprints
the EVAR proves dated activation of each named ravine
urban pluvial hazard may be reassigned to a natural ravine without component evidence
